title: Tailscale for KOReader
summary: A KOReader plugin that runs Tailscale on the e-reader, so Syncthing, SSH, and OPDS work from any network.
paragraphs: Many e-reader sync tools only work on a local network, which is awkward when your books live on a server at home. This plugin runs Tailscale inside KOReader, so the reader keeps a permanent Tailscale IP on any Wi-Fi network and Syncthing, SSH, or OPDS keep working.

My own testing has been on Kindle, but there are many platforms KoReader supports, and often it's only a matter of small file path fixes and library dependencies to get them working. Reported support has grown to include Kobo, Onyx, and Pocketbook.

title: SerialPM
summary: A project management app with a visual timeline, built as an SF State capstone.
paragraphs: SerialPM covers organisations, projects, tasks, team management, and real-time chat, with a visual timeline at the centre of each project. Led our team through an entire SDLC exercise, from requirements gathering to deployment, and brought various levels of web developmentabstraction to the other members to facilitate their contributions.
The public repository is a front-end showcase. The backend and database were built using real AWS resourcing that I've since deprecated.

title: Alzheimer’s screening experiment
summary: A random forest classifier on clinical data to identify likely Alzheimer’s diagnoses, optimized for recall.
paragraphs: An experiment in R that trains a random forest on clinical data to identify likely Alzheimer’s diagnoses.

In an experimental screening setting, we determined a missed case has a far steeper human cost than the model occasionally suggesting unneeded screenings, and found a recall-optimized model that outperformed our literature review baseline.

title: Auto Child Education
summary: A Europa Universalis V mod that picks each child’s education from their traits.
paragraphs: A mod for Europa Universalis V that removes the tedium of educating every child by hand. It scores each child’s traits and assigns the education that fits their strongest match.

I implemented the scoring model and tuned it against in-game behavior, using scripting to check for performance issues deeper into the games timeline (e.g., after 100 years of gameplay, there are *many* more children to manage). It has about 25,000 Steam Workshop subscribers.

title: geomat
summary: A MapLibre GL map of historical borders, with a timeline from late feudalism to the Cold War.
paragraphs: A MapLibre GL map with historical boundaries and a timeline from late feudalism to the Cold War. I really like playing with Google Maps & Earth, but I kind of want something like that for history & geography. I played with that idea a bit here.

title: Critique of the Gospel History of the Synoptics
summary: A machine translation of Bruno Bauer’s 1841 work of biblical criticism.
paragraphs: A machine translation of Bruno Bauer’s Kritik der evangelischen Geschichte der Synoptiker, a foundational text in German higher criticism.
The translation is offered for study and is credited with thanks to Vridar and Neil Godfrey.

title: Diablo II: Reimagined
summary: Contributed to a large community-driven mod for Diablo II: Resurrected that exhaustively brought modern ARPG mechanics to a Blizzard classic.
paragraphs: To do so, we worked with extremely old windows tooling and binaries; the lead developer has reverse engineered the game to a remarkable degree. I contributed to the mods item & rarity systems, helped move a 'corruption' mechanic into the mod that dynamically alters item properties (complexity never intended in the original), and maintained a rapid configuration system on the Discord for tech-literate users who wanted to customize their experience without touching legacy tooling. The mod has about 328,000 Nexus Mods downloads & 1,722 endorsements.
